body.statement: Determine the first nonzero normalization, leading limit or complete subsequential-limit set of \(\Delta_n\) along even \(n\), and decide whether \(\Delta_n=o(n^{-4/3})\). The construction must derive the two-coordinate hypergeometric boundary expansion before projecting to \(W\); no power law, constant, or parity law is prespecified.
body.justification: The finite threshold does not reveal the asymptotic price of count compression, which may live below the common second-order minimax scale.
body.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen derive the Airy correction for a shifted-binomial experiment; finite-population central limit theory does not resolve the finer bivariate-versus-projected decision risk.
body.consumer: A sharp scale would tell designers whether the finite information loss is practically persistent or asymptotically negligible relative to nonlinear shrinkage gains.

obligation.what_is_open: The first nonzero asymptotic normalization and the leading or subsequential limits of the balance-compression minimax tax remain open.
obligation.obstruction: Four finite games do not control the bivariate hypergeometric boundary layer or its projection uniformly as the even population size diverges.
obligation.attempted: The exact finite tax values and sandwich were derived; no uniform two-coordinate local expansion with remainder control follows from these certificates.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved finite certificates imply \(\Delta_2=\Delta_4=\Delta_6=0\) and
\[
 \Delta_8\geq L_8-U_8
 =\frac{4157665486237399704919833781773}
 {10670428130384321200748000000000000}
 >\frac{37}{100000}.
\]
They do not determine any normalization or subsequential limit of \(\Delta_n\) as \(n\) tends to infinity through even values.
